Definition: to yoke or hitch; by analogy, to fasten in any sense, to join battle
BiblicalUsage: This verb for binding — to tie, to yoke, to fasten — runs through the whole story. Joseph 'bound' Simeon before his brothers' eyes; a vow 'binds' the soul that makes it; the men of Judah 'bound' Samson with new ropes; and Elijah tells Ahab to harness — 'prepare' — his chariot before the rain.
TheologicalSignificance: Binding is sometimes judgment and sometimes duty: Simeon bound, Samson bound, a soul bound by its vow. I believe the word shows me that what I bind myself to matters — a vow is a chain I put on willingly, and God holds me to the words I speak.
